name: Two-thread conversation
description: Loop a conversation between two of your callable threads: each thread's reply becomes the other's next prompt, until an end marker, a max-exchange cap, or the time budget stops it.
notes: Both threads must be your own callable threads (nym.thread enforces ownership + the callable flag). Each reply is one AI call. The WALL CLOCK is the binding budget: an overrun is SIGKILLed and the transcript, which is delivered only after the loop, dies with it. The engine's real cap is invisible to the script and is NOT the declared 3600s on the tool path: there the wall clock is lowered to tool_timeout - 2 (298s by default) whatever the definition declares. So the recipe keeps its own clock and stops while it can still deliver, via time_budget_seconds (default 240, sized for that tool path). For a longer conversation run it headless (a recurring TODO, a trigger, or REST execute), which keeps the full 3600s budget, and raise time_budget_seconds to match. Delivers the transcript via nym.notify (long transcripts may be truncated by the delivery channel) and returns it. See the workflow-authoring cookbook.

workflow.source_code:
import time

# Coarse backstop only. The real governor is time_budget_seconds: the wall
# clock, not the call count, is what ends a run.
MAX_EXCHANGES = 20


def run(
    thread_a: str,
    thread_b: str,
    opening: str,
    max_exchanges: int = 6,
    end_marker: str = "[END CONVERSATION]",
    time_budget_seconds: int = 240,
):
    """Run an alternating conversation between two of your callable threads.

    Each thread's reply becomes the other thread's next prompt, so the two
    agents talk to each other. The loop stops when a reply contains end_marker,
    when max_exchanges replies have been produced, or when another reply would
    not fit inside time_budget_seconds.

    The recipe keeps its OWN clock because it cannot see the engine's. Delivery
    happens only after the loop, and a run that overruns its wall clock is
    SIGKILLed with the transcript still in the child's memory, so an overrun
    costs the whole conversation rather than just its last reply. The declared
    3600s budget is honored only on headless surfaces (a recurring TODO, a
    trigger, REST execute); on the tool path, which is what install_template
    binds to your thread, the engine silently lowers the run's wall clock to
    tool_timeout - 2 (298s by default) whatever the definition declares. So
    time_budget_seconds defaults to fit that smaller path and the loop stops
    while there is still room to deliver.

    Both threads must be your own callable threads (the nym.thread verb enforces
    ownership and the callable flag); pass their ids or callable names.

    Args:
        thread_a: Id or callable name of the first thread (must be yours, callable).
        thread_b: Id or callable name of the second thread (must be yours, callable).
        opening: The opening message that starts the exchange (sent to thread_a).
        max_exchanges: Maximum number of replies to produce (clamped to 1..20).
        end_marker: If a reply contains this exact text, the conversation ends.
        time_budget_seconds: Stop and deliver once another reply would not fit in
            this many seconds. Default 240, which fits the default tool-path wall
            clock. Raise it (toward 3500) only when running headless.
    """
    speakers = [thread_a, thread_b]
    exchanges = min(max(1, max_exchanges), MAX_EXCHANGES)
    budget_seconds = max(1, time_budget_seconds)
    transcript = []
    message = opening
    ended_by_marker = False
    ended_by_time = False
    started = time.monotonic()
    slowest_reply = 0.0
    for turn in range(exchanges):
        # Stop BEFORE a reply we cannot afford, using the slowest reply so far
        # as the estimate for the next one. The first reply always runs.
        if transcript and (time.monotonic() - started) + slowest_reply > budget_seconds:
            ended_by_time = True
            break
        speaker = speakers[turn % 2]
        prompt = (
            "You are having an ongoing conversation with another assistant. "
            "Read their latest message and reply with your next message only. "
            f"To end the conversation deliberately, include the exact text "
            f"{end_marker} anywhere in your reply.\n\n"
            f"Their message:\n{message}"
        )
        reply_started = time.monotonic()
        reply = str(nym.thread(prompt=prompt, id_or_title=speaker, mode="ask"))
        slowest_reply = max(slowest_reply, time.monotonic() - reply_started)
        transcript.append(f"[{speaker}]: {reply}")
        if end_marker in reply:
            ended_by_marker = True
            break
        message = reply
    if ended_by_time:
        stopped_by = "time budget"
    elif ended_by_marker:
        stopped_by = "end marker"
    else:
        stopped_by = "exchange cap"
    body = "\n\n".join(transcript)
    nym.notify(
        f"Two-thread conversation finished ({len(transcript)} replies, "
        f"stopped by {stopped_by}).\n\n{body}"
    )
    return {
        "replies": len(transcript),
        "ended_by_marker": ended_by_marker,
        "ended_by_time": ended_by_time,
        "transcript": transcript,
    }
